Why isn't my doctor's office showing up on Google Maps?

The SocialDMNov 11, 2026
Short answer

A doctor's office usually drops off Google Maps because its Google Business Profile is incomplete or inconsistent, it has fewer recent reviews than nearby practices, or Google can't tell its specialty. Maps ranks practices on relevance, distance and prominence.

The most common causes

  • The profile's primary category is too general, so you don't appear for your specialty.
  • Doctor and location listings aren't set up correctly, which splits or confuses your results.
  • Your name, address or phone number differs between your website, Google and directories like Healthgrades.
  • Nearby practices have more recent reviews than you do.
  • Your website doesn't clearly list conditions treated, procedures and the areas you serve.
  • Patients now ask AI tools like ChatGPT to recommend specialists, and those tools draw on the same signals.

What it costs you: patients searching "colorectal surgeon near me" or "dermatologist in Phoenix" choose from the first few results. If you are not there, referrals and self referred patients go to the practice that is.

How The SocialDM helps: LocalLift™ for medical practices checks how your practice shows up across Google, Maps, directories and AI search. It compares you with nearby practices and closes the gaps that keep patients from finding you. We focus on getting found, not on advertising claims.

FAQ

Can I pay Google to rank higher on Maps?

Ads can appear above the map results, but your regular map ranking can't be bought.

How long until we move up?

Timing depends on what is missing and how competitive your area is. We measure where you stand first, then report the change.

Do reviews really matter for doctors?

Yes. Recent reviews are one of the strongest local signals and one of the first things patients read.
